text: Near Loch Lomond, a six-vehicle collision has claimed the life of a 71-year-old biker riding a Harley Davidson equipped with a sidecar.
According to Leigh Hamilton, the ranger service manager for Loch Lomond National Park Authority, a fire that occurred in May due to a disposable barbecue at Glen Finglas had a "devastating impact."
One lorry crashed through the central reservation and collided with multiple lamp posts, while another unexpectedly released its load of beer barrels, resulting in damage to a bridge parapet as well.

The crash, involving a Range Rover, happened on the Ballymagowan Road at around 16:20 BST on Saturday, 7 June.
Police are continuing to appeal for information and dashcam footage from anyone who might have seen the crash or the car in the minutes before.
Sgt Luke Jenkins: If you were driving in the area and have a dash cam fitted, please review your footage as you may have captured something that could assist with our investigation.
Sgt Ewan Calder: I'd also ask drivers with dashcam footage to review this and bring anything of significance to our attention.
Officers are seeking witnesses to the crash or the moments leading up to it, and have appealed for any relevant dashcam, mobile or doorbell footage.
Doorbell and dashcam video footage is being sought by police investigating a serious crash, as a motorcyclist who was injured in it remains in hospital more than a week later.
The road has been shut for hours after the crash involving three lorries, two cars and a van at about 11:30 BST and is not expected to reopen between junctions one and 25 until 02:30 at the earliest.
